title: BigQuery: storage, compute and why they are billed apart

videos.script: Quitanda's analysts want to ask questions of every order ever placed. {{orders}} BigQuery answers them with no server to size. There is no cluster, no node type, nothing to switch off at night. {{nocluster}} What it has instead is two meters. One counts the bytes your tables hold, every month. {{storage}} The other counts the work your queries do. {{compute}} They are billed apart because they are apart. Storage is one system and compute is another, joined by Google's network. {{split}} BigQuery has no emulator. So you will generate two months of orders, about a million and a quarter, as Parquet files. {{generate}} DuckDB runs the SQL on those files. It cannot run BigQuery's bill, so you will work that out from Google's own sizes for each type. {{sizes}} Then the storage bill. For these orders it comes to nothing at all, and you will see why the query bill is the one to watch. {{bill}}
